whatItDoes: Adds sales tax to a pre-tax amount at the rate you enter, showing the tax amount and the total with tax. Works for any flat-rate tax, whether it's called sales tax, VAT, or GST.
whyItExists: Calculating sales tax by hand is easy to get wrong, especially for large purchases or unfamiliar rate brackets. An instant calculator gives an exact checkout total and makes budgeting precise.
whoShouldUse: Shoppers comparing prices after tax, freelance sellers adding tax to invoices, and anyone estimating the total cost of a purchase.
useCases: Estimate the final cost of a large purchase
Add the correct tax amount to an invoice
Compare prices after tax between states or products
Check how much of a total is actually tax
Budget for tax-inclusive online orders across regions
Verify a store's tax calculation on a receipt

Using the wrong local rate (county and city rates vary)
Tipping on the taxed total when some places tip pre-tax
Entering the rate without converting percent correctly
Applying the tax twice by accident
faq: Does this include other taxes? — No, it applies a single sales-tax rate to the pre-tax amount.
What is a typical rate? — Rates vary widely, commonly 0-12% depending on region.
Is it VAT or sales tax? — It works the same regardless of naming for a flat-rate tax.
Is my data shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
How is sales tax different from VAT? — Both are flat-rate taxes on a purchase; the mechanics differ across regions but the math is the same.
Is tax charged on shipping? — Some jurisdictions tax shipping and others don't; add shipping to the amount only if it's taxable where you buy.
